docs/design/command/README.md and docs/design/command/looks.json (for the shared Look format only)
description: PRD-002: Looks PoC. One Look format (catalogue keys only), Ember as the default Look across every screen, a 'Make it yours' Looks editor, saved/exported/imported Looks, Auto following the Look, and a live style page computed from the active Look. Stacked on the PRD-001 pilot. Zero changes to automatos-ai.

userStories.title: The Look format and catalogue
userStories.description: As a designer, I want one precise format for a Look so Looks can be saved, shared and checked.
acceptanceCriteria: All criteria of L-001 in docs/prd/PRD-002-LOOKS-POC.md: catalogue.ts (4 grounds, 6 accents with ink, 4 type styles, 4 shells with filter, 4 lights, values exactly as in the Ember Looks prototype), the fixed error #FF6B6B, types.ts (Look v1), presets.ts (Ember default, Obsidian, Aurora, Workshop, Daylight), and validate.ts (pure, typed result, rejects unknown keys, values outside the catalogue, glow outside 0–40, wrong schema, name/sub over 40 chars)
lib/looks/contrast.ts with the WCAG luminance/contrast helpers and readableOn() as specified in L-002 of the PRD (built here because the L-001 tests need it)

Tests: every preset validates; each rejection case; contrast for all 24 ground x accent pairs (text and text2 on bg and surface, ink on accent, readableOn(accent) and readableOn(error) on bg and surface, all >= 4.5:1)
docs/SKILL-GAPS.md gains a 'Design gaps' entry: raw accent and error colours as text fail AA on Paper (molten 2.49:1, error 2.41:1), fixed by the derived text colours
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Built lib/looks/{catalogue,types,presets,validate,contrast}.ts + tests/looks/*. Next stories: use validateLook() for every Look from storage/import, isKeyOf() for catalogue lookups, readableOn(colour, bg, surface, text) for --accent-text/--error-text (molten on Paper = #AA4C1C, error = #A54B49; PRD's 'about #A84A1B/#A84A49'). TypeStyle uses letterSpacing and sizes {hero, brand, status, card}; Shell uses filter.

userStories.title: Applying a Look
userStories.description: As a user, I want the whole app to change when I change the Look.
acceptanceCriteria: All criteria of L-002 in the PRD: lookToCssVars (including --accent-text and --error-text from readableOn), LookProvider (applies vars on the root, exposes look/setLook/saved/saveLook/deleteLook/renameLook, localStorage keys automatos-play.looks and automatos-play.look, every access in try/catch), and the pre-paint inline script in app/layout.tsx
prefers-reduced-motion is respected by the provider (a --motion variable or class the CSS uses to stop loops)
Tests: lookToCssVars for Ember; the provider switches variables and persists; corrupt or missing storage falls back to Ember
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Ember as the default, everywhere
userStories.description: As a user, I want Play to look like Ember out of the box.
acceptanceCriteria: All criteria of L-003 in the PRD: theme.css maps colour and display-type tokens to Look variables, the Ember fonts via @fontsource (no next/font/google), the Ember rules (serif display only and never below 19px, the radii, the glow crossfade, message rise, reduced motion), and every existing screen restyled to Ember
Text that shows the accent or error colour uses --accent-text / --error-text; fills, rings and icons use --accent / --error
A test scans app/ and components/ (.css, .tsx, .ts) for hex colour literals and fails on any outside lib/looks/catalogue.ts (test files and lib/looks/ excluded)
Existing tests from PRD-001 still pass (update selectors only where markup changed, never weaken an assertion)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Manage, export and import Looks

userStories.title: Auto follows the Look
userStories.description: As a user, I want Auto's shell and light to match my Look.
acceptanceCriteria: All criteria of L-006 in the PRD: the shell filter on the mascot video and PNG; ring colours (light for calm states, accent for busy states, error for oops, a dusk colour derived from the ground for sleeping and lost); Auto's light used only for the ring, eye glow and 'connected'
The ring-colour choice is a pure tested function of (state, look)
Tests: ring colour per state group under Ember and under Aurora; the filter for each of the 4 shells

userStories.title: The live style page
userStories.description: As a designer, I want to see exactly what my Look produces, with the numbers.
acceptanceCriteria: All criteria of L-007 in the PRD: app/looks/style/page.tsx linked from the Looks page; Colour (every token with name, hex, role, plus live contrast ratios with AA pass/fail as glyph plus word, including --accent-text and --error-text with a note when darkened), Type specimens, Spacing and radii drawn, the Components gallery (buttons, chips, tool lines, receipts, Deliverable card, message box, mascot slot in all 12 states with ring colours), Motion notes with a play toggle; Copy tokens as a :root block
Every value is computed from the active Look and redraws when it changes

Component tests: under Ember the page shows text/bg 16.36:1, text2/bg 8.54:1 and ink/molten 6.74:1 (each within 0.05); switching to Daylight changes the bg swatch and shows an accent text colour different from #FF6A1F
